residuals.title: CRC32C channel axiom (detected class proven, RFC-0228)
residuals.close: re-scoped by RFC-0228 (2026-09-15): the open part is ONLY the channel/hardware axiom — that NAND corruption lands inside the detected class. The class theorem is now PROVEN (formal/aeneas/lean/CrcClass.lean, zero sorry): every error E over GF(2)[X] that is a burst of length <= 32 bits, has odd Hamming weight, or is a 2-bit error with span < 2^31-1 satisfies not(G | E), with G = 0x11EDC6F41 = (X+1)*P31 (P31 = 0xF5B4253F); the order of X mod P31 is the prime 2^31-1, certified by a 30-step Frobenius chain of kernel-checked certificates (irreducibility of P31 is not needed for any of it). A blanket 'CRC32C never collides' claim remains FALSE by counting (2^(k) messages -> 2^32 CRCs for k > 32) and is NOT claimed. Code-level fail-closed behavior unchanged (crc_match mismatch => fail). Same class-axiom as VeriBetrKV; not a Pedra theorem. 0076 P2.2 crc_collision_admitted always false (crc_collision_axiom_remains); crc_match_ok is u32 equality, not a collision proof. 0081 P2.2 vlog_crc_collision_axiom_remains (same gate on VALUES.vlog / *.blob). 0082 P2.2 manifest_crc_collision_axiom_remains (LSM + history MANIFEST). 0083 P2.1 wal_open_crc_collision_axiom_remains. 0084 P2.1 checkpoint_crc_collision_axiom_remains. RFC-0155 names existing crc_match fail-closed inhabitant; never_floor row stays
